sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Cornflower is an annual of fields and open ground, native to temperate Europe and now widespread with cultivation or planted as an ornamental. It grows to about 75 cm; its blue flower heads are 3–4 cm across. The enlarged outer florets are sterile and form a funnel around the fertile central florets.

sections.title: Flowers and comparison
sections.text: Cornflower petals and florets are used as a garnish in some culinary settings; this does not apply to misidentified or treated plants. The plate correctly shows the blue head and narrow leaves. Unlike brown knapweed, Centaurea jacea, cornflower is annual and bright blue.
